replies.re: Make the app ready for real money (chair chat)
replies.body: Great news. Lots is already built and switched off: people connect their own Alpaca account (Alpaca holds the money, we never do), every trade is previewed and confirmed within 2 minutes, $1,000 cap per order, options only buy-to-open or sell-what-you-own (no spreads, nothing naked), saved logins are encrypted, every order logged, and an invite list decides who can trade. Still to do before real users: 1) Alpaca has to approve our app for other people's accounts (only you can apply). 2) Terms, privacy and a risk notice in the app (launch item 4 isn't built yet), plus 'not advice' and options-risk wording on idea cards, worded the way the lawyers cleared. 3) A full test on Alpaca's practice side: market closed, rejected order, part fills, selling, take-profit and stop-loss syncing. 4) Safety: stronger login for real-money accounts, a kill switch you can hit, a daily order limit. 5) Roll out slowly: you first on live, then a few invited people, then wider. The scheduled agents aren't allowed to touch real money, so this is for the build chat. I haven't switched anything on. I'm not a lawyer: check that the cleared scope covers the AI's 'Ways to play it' ideas for other people.

Good news: it's already most of the way to a phone app. The site can be added to the home screen today, opens full screen with its own icon, and can send price alerts. Three paths: 1) Home-screen app (what we have): free, no app store, every update is instant. Downside: people have to know to tap 'Add to Home Screen', and there's no store listing. 2) App-store wrapper: the same app put inside a thin shell (Capacitor) so it's in the Apple and Google stores. About 1-2 weeks of work, a $99/year Apple account and a $25 Google fee, and Apple's review. Apple often turns down apps that are just a website, so it needs a few phone-only extras (better alerts, Face ID, widgets). It also needs a closer look at the money rules, since this app touches trading. 3) Full native app (React Native or Swift): best feel, but basically a rebuild, months of work, and two codebases to keep up. My suggestion: stay on 1 while it's invite-only and polish the 'Add to Home Screen' prompt, then do 2 when you open it up. Nobody has started anything. Tell the build chat which one you want.
